issues.description: The template's private helper method singFarmSongVerse is declared without the Animal parameter (singFarmSongVerse(/*Animal animal*/)), while the problem UML and the solution implementation expect singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal). This mismatch in the method parameter will confuse students implementing singFarmSong() who will try to call singFarmSongVerse(animal) and encounter a signature mismatch or compilation error.
issues.suggestedFix: Update the template's singFarmSongVerse declaration to accept an Animal parameter (private void singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal)) so it matches the UML in the problem statement and the solution. Ensure the method body uses the passed animal and that singFarmSong() calls singFarmSongVerse(animal) for each animal.

issues.description: The problem statement and template refer to animal classes named Seal, Pig, and Goat, but the solution repository implements these as SpaceSeal, SpacePig, and SpaceGoat while leaving Goat.java, Pig.java, and Seal.java empty. This mismatch between expected class names (Seal/Pig/Goat) and the solution's actual types (Space-prefixed classes) can confuse students looking at the reference solution or comparing implementations.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the solution repository consistent with the problem statement: either implement and expose Seal, Pig, and Goat classes (with the specified interfaces and behavior) or update the problem statement and template to require SpaceSeal/SpacePig/SpaceGoat consistently. Remove or populate the empty Goat.java/Pig.java/Seal.java placeholders so the repository does not contain misleading empty files.

issues.description: The problem statement and the template refer to animal classes named Seal, Pig, and Goat, but the provided solution implementation uses differently named classes (SpaceSeal, SpacePig, SpaceGoat). This creates a mapping mismatch: students reading the problem and template expect to implement or interact with Seal/Pig/Goat, while the solution's concrete classes use a 'Space' prefix. The inconsistent class names for the same conceptual entities can confuse students trying to map requirements to the solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Use consistent class names across artifacts. Rename the solution classes to Seal, Pig, and Goat (or provide alias/adapter classes with these names) so they match the problem statement and template Main.java, or update the problem statement and template to explicitly use the Space-prefixed names and explain the naming choice.
